whyEn: Exam weight 2/3. This chapter is short on pages but dense on testable numbers: the epinephrine dose (and how BC's fixed adult dose differs from the textbook's weight-based formula), the two epinephrine concentrations, the biphasic-reaction time window, and the fixed drug sequence (epinephrine before salbutamol or diphenhydramine, always) are all classic COPR items. It also drives a practical-exam scenario directly: anaphylaxis is on BC's automatic 'unstable' list regardless of vitals.
whyZh: 考试权重 2/3。这一章篇幅不长，但数字密度很高：肾上腺素剂量（以及 BC 固定成人剂量和教材按体重公式的区别）、两种浓度的区分、双相反应的时间窗、以及固定的给药顺序（永远先肾上腺素，后沙丁胺醇或苯海拉明）都是 COPR 笔试的常客。它也直接决定实操站的走向：无论生命体征如何，过敏性休克在 BC 都自动判定为「不稳定」。

sections.titleEn: Introduction: An Immune System Turned Against Itself
sections.titleZh: 引言：一套反噬自己的免疫系统

points.en: The term anaphylaxis dates to 1902, coined by Portier and Richet from Greek for 'without protection' after a sensitized dog died on a second exposure to sea anemone toxin instead of being protected by it.
points.zh: anaphylaxis 一词诞生于 1902 年，Portier 和 Richet 用希腊语「无防护」命名——因为一只已致敏的狗在第二次接触海葵毒素时不但没被保护，反而死了。

points.en: The 2006 U.S. NIAID definition to memorize: anaphylaxis is a serious allergic reaction that is rapid in onset and may cause death.
points.zh: 要背的定义（2006 年美国 NIAID）：anaphylaxis 是一种起病急、可能致死的严重过敏反应。

points.en: In Canada roughly 1 person in 3 million dies of anaphylaxis each year, and in up to two-thirds of cases no trigger is ever identified.
points.zh: 加拿大每年约 300 万人中有 1 人死于过敏性休克；其中多达三分之二的病例始终找不到诱因。

points.en: Anaphylaxis has no age immunity — documented cases range from a 6-month-old infant to an 89-year-old adult, with no clear sex or race predilection.
points.zh: 过敏性休克不挑年龄——有记录的病例小到 6 个月大婴儿，大到 89 岁老人，也没有明显的性别或种族倾向。

points.en: Most anaphylaxis deaths come from brain hypoxia or from complications of the epinephrine treatment itself, not from the allergy in isolation — which is exactly why correct dosing matters as much as giving the drug at all.
points.zh: 过敏性休克致死大多是脑缺氧或肾上腺素治疗本身的并发症，而不是过敏反应单独造成的——这正是为什么剂量给对，和给不给药同样重要。

sections.titleEn: Pathophysiology: How IgE Ignites a Whole-Body Storm
sections.titleZh: 病理生理：IgE 如何点燃全身风暴

points.en: The immune system runs on two tracks: cellular immunity (T cells attack invaders directly) and humoral immunity (B cells manufacture antibodies, or immunoglobulins, against surface antigens).
points.zh: 免疫系统靠两条线运作：细胞免疫（T 细胞直接攻击入侵者）和体液免疫（B 细胞针对表面抗原制造抗体，也就是免疫球蛋白）。

points.en: IgE is the antibody that matters for allergy and anaphylaxis — it sits on mast cells and basophils, unlike IgG (fights bacteria/viruses, triggers complement) or IgM (first antibody to appear, drives ABO agglutination).
points.zh: 过敏和过敏性休克真正的主角是 IgE——它就驻扎在肥大细胞和嗜碱性粒细胞表面；对比 IgG（抗菌抗病毒、激活补体）和 IgM（最先出现、驱动 ABO 血型凝集）。

points.en: Most allergic reactions and anaphylaxis are Type I hypersensitivity: an immediate reaction that requires prior sensitization — the first encounter primes IgE production, and only a later re-exposure to that same allergen sets off the reaction.
points.zh: 多数过敏和过敏性休克属于 I 型超敏反应：一种即时反应，前提是已经被致敏过——第一次接触只是给 IgE 打底，真正发作要等到再一次接触同一种过敏原。

points.en: On re-exposure, IgE orders mast cells and basophils to dump proinflammatory mediators, histamine chief among them — injecting histamine alone can reproduce most of the symptoms seen in anaphylaxis.
points.zh: 再次接触时，IgE 指挥肥大细胞和嗜碱性粒细胞倾泻炎症介质，组胺是主角——单独注射组胺就能复制出过敏性休克的大部分症状。

points.en: Histamine's four-front assault: vascular permeability up (capillary leak drives angioedema and urticaria), bronchoconstriction plus mucus (airway), vasodilation plus myocardial depression (hypotension and dysrhythmia), and gut smooth-muscle contraction (cramping, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea).
points.zh: 组胺同时四线开打：血管通透性升高（毛细血管渗漏→血管性水肿和荨麻疹）、支气管收缩加分泌物增多（气道）、血管扩张加心肌抑制（低血压和心律失常）、肠道平滑肌收缩（绞痛、恶心、呕吐、腹泻）。

points.en: The capillary leak can be dramatic: as much as 50% of circulating vascular volume can shift into extravascular tissue within just 10 minutes of allergen exposure — the physiologic reason anaphylactic hypotension can hit so suddenly.
points.zh: 毛细血管渗漏可以很夸张：接触过敏原后短短 10 分钟内，多达 50% 的循环血容量就能转移到血管外组织——这正是过敏性休克血压能垮得这么快的生理学原因。

points.en: Top triggers by category: medications lead overall (penicillin/beta-lactams/cephalosporins are the single most common cause; neuromuscular blockers cause 50-70% of anaphylaxis seen during anaesthesia); insect stings (bee, wasp, hornet, fire ant) cause a systemic reaction in 0.5-3% of people stung.
points.zh: 各类诱因之首：药物总体最常见（青霉素类/β-内酰胺类/头孢类是头号原因；神经肌肉阻滞剂占麻醉相关过敏性休克的 50-70%）；昆虫叮咬（蜂类、黄蜂、大黄蜂、火蚁）中约 0.5-3% 的被蜇者会出现全身反应。

points.en: Foods are the most common prehospital cause of anaphylaxis and carry a disproportionately high fatality rate: peanuts, tree nuts, and shellfish across all ages; cow's milk, wheat, soy, and egg more often in children — as little as 100 mcg of peanut protein can set off a reaction.
points.zh: 食物是院前过敏性休克最常见的诱因，致死率也偏高：花生、坚果、贝类各年龄段都常见；牛奶、小麦、大豆、鸡蛋则在儿童中更多见——花生蛋白哪怕只有 100 mcg 都可能诱发反应。

points.en: A localized reaction to a sting is NOT itself a risk factor for anaphylaxis — but a patient who develops generalized urticaria after a sting is at meaningfully higher risk of a systemic reaction.
points.zh: 被蜇后只是局部反应，本身并不算过敏性休克的风险因素——但如果被蜇后出现全身性荨麻疹，发生系统性反应的风险就明显更高。

points.en: Epinephrine is essentially histamine's mirror-image antidote: it vasoconstricts, boosts heart rate and contractility, bronchodilates, and suppresses further mediator release from mast cells and basophils — reversing all four fronts of the histamine assault at once.
points.zh: 肾上腺素基本就是组胺的镜像解药：它收缩血管、提升心率和收缩力、扩张支气管、并抑制肥大细胞和嗜碱性粒细胞继续放出介质——一次性逆转组胺四条战线上的破坏。

points.en: Nancy's teaching point: the word anaphylaxis literally means 'without protection,' but the real pathophysiology is the opposite — a protective immune system that has gone catastrophically overboard.
points.zh: Nancy 的点睛之笔：anaphylaxis 字面意思是「无防护」，但真正的病理生理恰恰相反——是一套本该保护身体的免疫系统，防护过了头、彻底失控。

sections.titleEn: Clinical Symptoms of Anaphylaxis and the Biphasic Trap
sections.titleZh: 临床表现与双相反应的陷阱

points.en: Classic presentation is rash plus respiratory symptoms plus hypotension in any combination; GI symptoms (cramping, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) are common too but easily missed because a patient fixated on one symptom may not volunteer the others unless you ask directly.
points.zh: 典型表现是皮疹＋呼吸道症状＋低血压，三者可以任意组合出现；消化道症状（绞痛、恶心、呕吐、腹泻）也很常见，但容易漏问——病人往往只盯着最难受的那一个症状，不追问就不会主动说其他的。

points.en: System-by-system picture: skin (flushed, itchy, hives, swelling of face/tongue/hands/feet); respiratory (dyspnea, throat/chest tightness, stridor, hoarseness, wheeze, crackles, cough, sneeze); cardiovascular (dysrhythmia, hypotension, tachycardia); GI (cramping, bloating, vomiting, watery diarrhea); CNS (headache, dizziness, confusion, anxiety, sense of impending doom, syncope) — dyspnea, hypotension, and tachycardia are flagged as the three key indicators.
points.zh: 逐系统清单：皮肤（潮红、瘙痒、荨麻疹、面部/舌/手脚肿胀）；呼吸（呼吸困难、咽喉胸部发紧、喉鸣、声嘶、喘鸣、湿啰音、咳嗽、喷嚏）；心血管（心律失常、低血压、心动过速）；消化道（绞痛、腹胀、呕吐、水样腹泻）；中枢神经（头痛、头晕、意识混乱、焦虑、濒死感、晕厥）——呼吸困难、低血压、心动过速被列为三大关键指标。

points.en: Exposure route predicts severity: injected or ingested allergens tend to trigger more severe reactions than contact or inhaled exposure.
points.zh: 暴露途径决定严重度：注射或吞食入体的过敏原，往往比接触或吸入的反应更重。

points.en: Death-timing by route is a striking exam number: fatalities from ingested allergens occur around 30 minutes after exposure on average, from insect stings around 15 minutes, and from iatrogenic (injected) allergens around 5 minutes — the more direct the route, the faster the clock runs.
points.zh: 按暴露途径统计的致死时间是个很抓眼的考点：吞食性过敏原致死平均约在暴露后 30 分钟，昆虫叮咬约 15 分钟，医源性注射约 5 分钟——途径越直接，倒计时越快。

points.en: Biphasic reaction defined: an initial-phase response (vasodilation, vascular leak, smooth-muscle spasm) starts within the first 30 minutes of exposure and typically resolves within about 1 hour; a delayed second-phase response can follow hours later and last for days, driven by heavier inflammatory-cell infiltration and sometimes worse than the first wave.
points.zh: 双相反应定义：起初的第一相反应（血管扩张、血管渗漏、平滑肌痉挛）在暴露后 30 分钟内开始，通常约 1 小时内消退；数小时之后可能出现延迟的第二相反应，能持续数天，由更强的炎症细胞浸润驱动，有时比第一波更严重。

points.en: Anaphylaxis can also simply be protracted (dragging on for days) or delayed in onset (symptoms starting well after the exposure) — a quiet first hour never rules it out.
points.zh: 过敏性休克还可能单纯拖成慢性（持续数天）或延迟起病（暴露很久之后才发作）——第一个小时安静，不代表可以排除。

points.en: Atopy loads the dice: 1/3 to 1/2 of anaphylaxis patients have a personal history of atopic disease (allergic rhinitis, asthma, atopic dermatitis), and about half of those also have a positive family history — but a clean personal and family history never excludes the diagnosis.
points.zh: 特应性体质会加大风险：三分之一到二分之一的过敏性休克病人有特应性疾病史（过敏性鼻炎、哮喘、特应性皮炎），其中约一半还有阳性家族史——但个人和家族史都干净，也不能排除诊断。

points.en: Other severity risk factors: peanut/tree-nut allergy (especially in adolescents), pre-existing respiratory or cardiovascular disease, asthma, delayed epinephrine administration, a prior biphasic reaction, advanced age, and mast cell disease.
points.zh: 其他加重严重度的风险因素：花生/坚果过敏（青少年尤其明显）、既往呼吸或心血管疾病、哮喘、肾上腺素给药延迟、既往有过双相反应、高龄、以及肥大细胞病。

points.en: Diagnostic criteria — any ONE of three patterns counts as anaphylaxis: (1) acute skin/mucosal involvement plus respiratory compromise, falling BP, or end-organ dysfunction; (2) two or more systems involved rapidly after a likely-allergen exposure; (3) hypotension alone after a KNOWN allergen exposure.
points.zh: 诊断标准——满足以下任意一条即可判为过敏性休克：①急性皮肤/黏膜受累＋呼吸受损、血压下降或终末器官功能障碍其一；②接触疑似过敏原后迅速累及两个或以上系统；③已知过敏原暴露后仅出现血压下降。

points.en: Criterion 3's BP thresholds, adult vs pediatric: adult systolic BP under 90 mm Hg or a drop of 30% or more from baseline; pediatric age-specific low systolic BP, or a drop of more than 30%.
points.zh: 第③条的血压切点，成人 vs 儿童：成人收缩压 <90 mm Hg 或较基线下降 ≥30%；儿童按年龄段的低收缩压标准，或下降超过 30%。

points.en: Criterion 3 exists specifically to catch the rare patient whose ONLY sign is severe hypotension after a known allergen — skin findings are not a required element of the diagnosis.
points.zh: 第③条专门用来抓住那种极少数、唯一表现就是严重低血压的病人——皮肤表现并不是诊断的必要条件。

sections.titleEn: Assessment: ABCs on a Fast-Closing Window
sections.titleZh: 评估：在快速关闭的窗口里做 ABC

points.en: Assessment and treatment often have to happen simultaneously in anaphylaxis — a patient who looks stable can crash within minutes, so keep your index of suspicion high whenever any allergy-pattern symptom is present.
points.zh: 过敏性休克里评估和处置往往要同步进行——看起来还稳的病人可能几分钟内就崩；只要出现任何一点过敏模式的症状，就要保持高度怀疑。

points.en: Airway red flags demanding immediate action: angioedema of lips or tongue, stridor or hoarseness from severe laryngeal/epiglottic swelling, a reported 'lump in the throat', or frequent coughing/sneezing to try to clear it — any of these should trigger epinephrine and airway stabilization right away, not a wait-and-see approach.
points.zh: 需要立刻动手的气道红旗：唇舌血管性水肿、喉/会厌重度肿胀导致的喉鸣或声嘶、病人主诉「喉咙有东西堵着」、或频繁咳嗽打喷嚏想清嗓子——出现任何一条都该立刻给肾上腺素、稳定气道，不能观望等待。

points.en: Prepare for a difficult airway before you need it: select a smaller ET tube than usual, landmark and set up cricothyrotomy equipment in advance, and be ready to move to a surgical airway immediately if intubation fails — edema, secretions, and bronchospasm can defeat both BVM ventilation and intubation.
points.zh: 提前为困难气道做准备：选比平时更小号的气管插管、提前定位并备好环甲膜切开器材、插管失败就立刻转外科气道——水肿、分泌物和支气管痉挛能同时废掉球囊面罩通气和气管插管。

points.en: An absent wheeze is NOT reassurance in anaphylaxis — it can mean so little air is moving (fatigue, severe edema, mucus plugging) that turbulent airflow can no longer generate the sound; a silent chest is a dangerous sign, not an improving one.
points.zh: 过敏性休克里听不到喘鸣不代表在好转——可能是气流太弱（疲劳、严重水肿、痰堵）已经小到发不出声音；「沉默的胸腔」是危险信号，不是好消息。

points.en: Breathing treatment order: high-flow oxygen and salbutamol nebulization help bronchospasm, but epinephrine remains the drug of choice for bronchodilation; in severe airway edema, nebulized epinephrine has also shown benefit.
points.zh: 呼吸处置顺序：高流量吸氧和沙丁胺醇雾化能缓解支气管痉挛，但支气管扩张的首选药始终是肾上腺素；重度气道水肿时，雾化肾上腺素也显示出效果。

points.en: Circulation clues: tachycardia, hypotension, and frank shock are all possible; pallor, cyanosis, and confusion from cerebral hypoperfusion can appear — and in a rare subset of patients, hypotension/shock is the ONLY sign of anaphylaxis, with no rash at all.
points.zh: 循环线索：心动过速、低血压、明显休克都可能出现；脑灌注不足会带来面色苍白、发绀和意识混乱——极少数病人身上，低血压/休克是过敏性休克唯一的表现，完全没有皮疹。

points.en: Fluid math (book reference): because leaked plasma volume is large, patients may need roughly 1-2 L of IV crystalloid (NS or LR) up front; escalate to a vasopressor if there's no response after 3-4 L.
points.zh: 补液参考量（教材数字）：因为漏出的血浆量很大，病人前期可能需要约 1-2 L 静脉晶体液（生理盐水或乳酸林格液）；如果给到 3-4 L 仍无反应，就该考虑升压药。

points.en: Cardiac dysrhythmias can arise both from anaphylaxis itself and as a known complication of epinephrine administration — cardiac monitoring is mandatory, not optional, once epinephrine is on board.
points.zh: 心律失常既可能是过敏性休克本身造成的，也是肾上腺素给药已知的并发症——一旦用了肾上腺素，心电监护就不是可选项，而是必须项。

points.en: Any deterioration in mental status (confusion, restlessness, agitation sliding toward obtundation) should immediately trigger epinephrine plus an airway re-check — it signals worsening shock or cerebral hypoxia, not simple anxiety.
points.zh: 意识状态任何一点恶化（意识混乱、烦躁不安、逐渐昏睡）都该立刻触发肾上腺素给药加气道复查——这提示休克或脑缺氧在恶化，而不是单纯焦虑。

points.en: Scene clues point straight at the trigger: a garden nearby suggests a possible sting, a seafood dinner suggests a possible shellfish reaction — reading the scene both narrows the diagnosis now and shapes patient-education advice later.
points.zh: 现场线索能直接指向诱因：附近有花园就要怀疑叮咬，晚餐是海鲜就要怀疑贝类过敏——读懂现场既能当下缩小诊断范围，也为之后的患者教育提供依据。

points.en: History must probe prior reaction severity and treatment already given: a patient with a known life-threatening peanut history who is re-exposed gets epinephrine immediately without waiting for symptoms to build; and remember exposure can precede symptom onset by hours.
points.zh: 问病史要问既往反应有多重、以及已经用过什么药：已知有致命花生反应史的病人一旦再次暴露，不必等症状出现就该立刻给肾上腺素；同时要记住，暴露到发病之间可能间隔数小时。

points.en: Medication history reshapes what you're seeing: prior antihistamine use may mask a rash; prior self-administered EpiPen or salbutamol changes the timeline and what to expect next; beta-blocker use can blunt the epinephrine response and mask the expected tachycardia — ask about all three every time.
points.zh: 用药史会改变你看到的表现：已经用过抗组胺药可能没有皮疹；已经自己打过 EpiPen 或用过沙丁胺醇会改变时间线和接下来的预期；用 β 受体阻滞剂会削弱肾上腺素效果、还可能掩盖本该出现的心动过速——这三项每次都要问。

points.en: Ongoing assessment happens en route: repeat ABCs and serial vitals, keep an extra IM epinephrine dose drawn up in anticipation of deterioration, mentally rehearse a difficult airway, and secure or add a second IV line.
points.zh: 持续评估放在转运途中做：反复检查 ABC 和连续生命体征、预先抽好备用的肌注肾上腺素以防恶化、脑中预演困难气道流程、并确保或加开第二条静脉通路。

sections.titleEn: Management: Epinephrine First, Everything Else After
sections.titleZh: 处置：肾上腺素永远排第一，其他都在后面

points.en: Epinephrine reversal mechanism: it is the ONLY drug that reverses anaphylaxis itself — vasoconstriction, improved cardiac contractility, bronchodilation, and suppression of further mediator release, all at once; there is no absolute contraindication to epinephrine in a life-threatening anaphylactic reaction.
points.zh: 肾上腺素的逆转机制：它是唯一能逆转过敏性休克本身的药——血管收缩、心肌收缩力增强、支气管扩张、抑制介质继续释放，四件事同时发生；在危及生命的过敏性休克里，肾上腺素没有绝对禁忌证。

points.en: BC adult IM epinephrine dosing: 0.5 mg IM of the 1:1,000 solution, at the anterolateral thigh, may repeat every 5 minutes up to 3 doses total for anaphylaxis.
points.zh: BC 成人肌注肾上腺素剂量：1:1,000 浓度 0.5 mg 肌注，大腿前外侧，可每 5 分钟重复一次，过敏性休克最多共 3 次。

points.en: BC pediatric IM epinephrine dosing: 0.01 mg/kg IM to a maximum of 0.5 mg, may repeat up to 3 times — same repeat cap as the adult dose, but weight-based rather than fixed.
points.zh: BC 儿童肌注肾上腺素剂量：0.01 mg/kg 肌注，上限 0.5 mg，可重复最多 3 次——重复次数上限和成人一致，但按体重算而不是固定值。

points.en: The textbook's underlying weight-based formula is broader: 0.01 mg/kg IM (max 0.5 mg adult / 0.3 mg pediatric) at the anterolateral thigh, repeatable every 5-15 minutes as needed — know both this formula and BC's fixed 0.5 mg adult exam answer.
points.zh: 教材背后的按体重公式覆盖面更宽：0.01 mg/kg 肌注（成人上限 0.5 mg，儿童上限 0.3 mg），大腿前外侧，按需每 5-15 分钟可重复——这个公式和 BC 固定 0.5 mg 的成人考试答案都要记住。

points.en: Auto-injector fixed doses differ from the protocol dose: an adult EpiPen delivers 0.3 mg IM, while the pediatric EpiPen delivers 0.15 mg IM and is intended for children weighing 15-30 kg — most adults (over 50 kg) can still safely receive the larger 0.5 mg protocol dose.
points.zh: 自带笔式注射器的固定剂量和协议剂量不同：成人 EpiPen 一次给 0.3 mg 肌注，儿童版 EpiPen 给 0.15 mg 肌注，适用于 15-30 kg 的儿童——大多数成人（体重 >50 kg）仍能安全接受更大的 0.5 mg 协议剂量。

points.en: Concentration trap: 1:1,000 (1 mg/mL) is the IM concentration used for anaphylaxis; 1:10,000 (0.1 mg/mL) — 10 times more dilute — is the IV/cardiac-arrest concentration; pushing a full 1-mL vial of the 1:1,000 concentration IV is a lethal-overdose error.
points.zh: 浓度陷阱：1:1,000（1 mg/mL）是肌注用于过敏性休克的浓度；1:10,000（0.1 mg/mL，稀释 10 倍）是静脉/心脏骤停用的浓度；把 1:1,000 整支 1 mL 直接静推是致命的过量错误。

points.en: IV epinephrine (book reference) is reserved for refractory shock or peri-arrest: dilute 1 mL of the 1:10,000 vial into 10 mL saline and give 0.05-0.1 mg slow IV, or run an infusion at 1-4 mcg/min (1 mg in 250 mL saline = 4 mcg/mL) — treat this as background knowledge alongside BC's IM-only anaphylaxis protocol.
points.zh: 静脉肾上腺素（教材参考）留给难治性休克或濒临骤停：把 1 支 1:10,000 稀释成 1 mL 加 10 mL 生理盐水后缓慢静推 0.05-0.1 mg，或以 1-4 mcg/min 持续输注（1 mg 加进 250 mL 生理盐水＝4 mcg/mL）——这部分作为背景知识记住，BC 的过敏性休克协议本身只写肌注。

points.en: IM beats subcutaneous and default IV-bolus dosing: IM gives faster, more reliable absorption than SC, and IV bolus dosing has been linked to dosing errors, dysrhythmias, and deaths — so IM stays first-line even once IV access is already running.
points.zh: 肌注优于皮下注射，也优于常规静推：肌注吸收比皮下更快更稳，而静推给药已被证实和用药错误、心律失常、死亡相关——所以哪怕静脉通路已经开好，肌注依然是首选。

points.en: Sequencing rule (a major protocol-error trap): salbutamol treats bronchospasm and diphenhydramine (25-50 mg IM/IV, given slowly) blunts the histamine response — but BOTH come AFTER epinephrine, never instead of it.
points.zh: 给药顺序（重大协议错误陷阱）：沙丁胺醇处理支气管痉挛，苯海拉明（25-50 mg 肌注/静注、缓慢给药）抑制组胺反应——但两者都必须排在肾上腺素之后，绝不能替代它。

points.en: Corticosteroids (methylprednisolone, hydrocortisone, dexamethasone) act too slowly to help the acute crisis — their theoretical role is blunting a later/biphasic reaction, not reversing the immediate life threat.
points.zh: 皮质类固醇（甲泼尼龙、氢化可的松、地塞米松）起效太慢，帮不上急性期——它们理论上的作用是压制后续的双相反应，而不是逆转当下的致命威胁。

points.en: Beta-blocker patients are a known trap: they can have more severe, more frequent anaphylaxis and a paradoxical (blunted) response to epinephrine; glucagon (1-5 mg IV over 5 minutes, then an infusion of 5-15 mg/min per the textbook) and ipratropium are the classic rescue options — protect the airway first since nausea/vomiting is a major glucagon side effect.
points.zh: 用 β 受体阻滞剂的病人是已知陷阱：他们的过敏性休克可能更重更频繁，对肾上腺素还可能出现反常（削弱）反应；教材给出的经典补救是胰高血糖素（1-5 mg 静注、用时 5 分钟，之后可 5-15 mg/min 持续输注）和异丙托溴铵——用之前先护好气道，因为恶心呕吐是胰高血糖素的主要副作用。

points.en: Refractory shock beyond epinephrine: continued aggressive fluids, second-line vasopressors (norepinephrine/vasopressin), and — where available — ECMO; call the receiving ED early if the patient isn't responding to standard treatment.
points.zh: 肾上腺素之外的难治性休克处理：继续积极补液、二线升压药（去甲肾上腺素/血管加压素）、有条件时甚至考虑 ECMO——病人对标准治疗没反应时，要尽早联系接收医院。

points.en: BC fluid bolus for anaphylactic hypotension: crystalloid 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L, reassessing after every 500 mL — this replaces the book's looser '1-2 L up front, escalate past 3-4 L' guidance as the exam answer.
points.zh: BC 对过敏性休克低血压的补液标准：晶体液 20 mL/kg、上限 2 L、每 500 mL 复评一次——这是考试答案，取代教材那种「先给 1-2 L、超过 3-4 L 再升级」的宽泛说法。

points.en: Non-drug BC protocol steps come first and are explicit: position the patient supine and never let them walk (orthostatic stress can crash a marginal BP further), physically remove the ongoing allergen source (scrape a stinger, stop an infusion), and delegate a crew member to prep the egress route while treatment continues.
points.zh: BC 协议里明确要求先做的非药物步骤：让病人仰卧、绝不让其行走（体位性应激可能把本就勉强的血压彻底压垮）、物理移除仍在持续的过敏原（刮掉蜂刺、停掉输液），并指派一名搭档在继续治疗的同时准备撤离路线。

points.en: Psychological support is clinically relevant, not just kind: many patients recognize how serious their situation is, and unmanaged anxiety adds its own catecholamine surge — staying calm and narrating your actions is part of the treatment.
points.zh: 心理安抚有临床意义，不只是礼貌：很多病人清楚自己的情况有多严重，没被安抚的焦虑本身也会带来一波额外的儿茶酚胺——保持冷静、边做边说，本身就是治疗的一部分。

points.en: Every hypersensitivity-reaction patient should be strongly encouraged to go to hospital, even with mild symptoms — up to 20% of patients have a symptom recurrence within the next 8 hours despite an initially good response to treatment.
points.zh: 每一个过敏反应病人都该被强烈建议送医，哪怕症状很轻——多达 20% 的病人在治疗初期反应良好后，仍会在接下来 8 小时内症状复发。

points.en: In BC, anaphylaxis itself is on the explicit list of automatic 'unstable' findings for the practical exam — regardless of current vital signs, it is treated and transported as an unstable RTC.
points.zh: 在 BC，过敏性休克本身就明确列在实操考的自动「不稳定」清单里——无论当前生命体征如何，都按不稳定 RTC 处理和转运。

points.en: In-hospital observation windows run roughly 4-8 hours depending on clinical severity before a symptom-free patient is discharged; every discharged patient should leave with a filled or fillable EpiPen prescription, because future severity can never be predicted from today's reaction.
points.zh: 院内观察时长大约 4-8 小时，视临床严重度而定，无症状后才能出院；每个出院病人都该带走一份已配或可配的 EpiPen 处方——因为今天反应的轻重，预测不了下一次。

points.en: Escalate transport priority or call for additional resources whenever the patient's needs exceed what's available on scene — airway difficulty, refractory shock, or the need for advanced-airway backup are all valid triggers.
points.zh: 只要病人的需求超出现场能力，就该提高转运优先级或呼叫增援——气道困难、难治性休克、或需要高级气道支援都算触发条件。

points.en: Core teaching points before you leave: how to identify and avoid the specific antigen — including alternate or cross-reacting names (e.g., other penicillin-family drugs) — and the need to tell every future health-care provider about the allergy, not just their regular doctor.
points.zh: 离开前的核心教育点：如何识别并避开具体过敏原——包括别名和交叉反应药物（比如其他青霉素类药物）——以及要告知未来遇到的每一位医护人员，而不只是自己的家庭医生。

points.en: Medical alert jewelry (bracelet or tag) protects patients who can't speak for themselves during a future reaction — it is often the only history a crew gets from an unresponsive patient.
points.zh: 医疗警示手环或吊牌能在未来病人说不出话时替他说话——对无反应的病人来说，这常常是急救人员能拿到的唯一病史来源。

points.en: Anaphylaxis-kit advice: carry it at all times, and consider carrying two doses (or a kit with more than one dose) since many reactions need more than a single epinephrine dose — and make sure both the patient and family actually know how to use it.
points.zh: 随身急救包建议：随时带着，并考虑带两支（或含多剂量的套装），因为很多反应需要不止一次肾上腺素——同时确保病人和家属真的会用它，而不只是带着。

points.en: Teach early reporting: symptoms should be reported and treated before they become life-threatening, and patients should understand that repeated exposures can produce faster, more severe reactions than the last one.
points.zh: 教患者早报告：应该在症状变得致命之前就报告和处理，也要让病人明白反复暴露可能让反应比上一次更快、更重。

points.en: Biphasic-reaction education is a required teaching point: warn patients they may develop a delayed second wave of symptoms, and recommend monitoring for up to 4-8 hours after the initial anaphylactic event.
points.zh: 双相反应教育是必讲内容：告诉病人可能会出现延迟的第二波症状，建议在首次过敏性休克发作后监测 4-8 小时。

atScene.en: Scan for the trigger the moment you walk in — a garden visible outside suggests a possible sting, a table full of shellfish suggests a possible food trigger; identifying the source drives both immediate care and later patient education.
atScene.zh: 一进门就扫一眼找诱因——外面看到花园就要怀疑叮咬，桌上摆满贝类就要怀疑食物过敏；认出来源既能指导当下处置，也是之后患者教育的素材。

atScene.en: Position supine, never let the patient walk, and physically remove the ongoing exposure (scrape a stinger, stop a drug infusion) before anything else — these are explicit first steps in BC's Anaphylaxis guideline.
atScene.zh: 先仰卧、绝不让病人走、并物理移除仍在持续的暴露（刮掉蜂刺、停掉输液）——这些是 BC 过敏性休克指南里明写的最前面几步。

atScene.en: If a stridorous or hoarse patient can still speak, high-flow O2 by nonrebreathing mask plus a position of comfort may be all the immediate airway management needed — but reassess constantly, because the clinical course over the next hours is unpredictable.
atScene.zh: 有喉鸣或声嘶但仍能说话的病人，非重复呼吸面罩高流量给氧加舒适体位可能就是当下需要的全部气道处理——但要持续复评，因为接下来几小时的病程无法预测。

atScene.en: An absent wheeze in a patient working this hard to breathe is not good news — it can mean too little air is moving to make noise; treat a silent chest as more dangerous, not less.
atScene.zh: 呼吸这么费力却听不到喘鸣不是好消息——可能是气流太弱到发不出声音；把「沉默的胸腔」当成更危险，而不是更轻。

atScene.en: Ask specifically about beta-blocker use, prior EpiPen or salbutamol self-administration (and when), and antihistamine use — each answer changes what you're seeing and what you should expect from your epinephrine.
atScene.zh: 要专门问：是否用 β 受体阻滞剂、之前是否自己用过 EpiPen 或沙丁胺醇（什么时候）、以及是否用过抗组胺药——每一个答案都会改变你眼前看到的情况和肾上腺素的预期效果。

atScene.en: Delegate a crew member to prep the egress route the moment you recognize anaphylaxis — BC's protocol names this explicitly, because minutes matter once you commit to transport.
atScene.zh: 一旦认出过敏性休克就立刻指派一名搭档准备撤离路线——BC 协议明确写出这一条，因为一旦决定转运，分秒都很值钱。

atScene.en: Draw up a second dose of epinephrine as soon as the first is given — don't wait for deterioration to start preparing.
atScene.zh: 第一剂肾上腺素给出去的同时就该抽好第二剂——别等病情恶化了才开始准备。

confusions.en: 'No rash, no anaphylaxis' — wrong: a rare subset of patients present with hypotension or shock as the only sign; skin findings are not a required element of the diagnostic criteria.
confusions.zh: 「没皮疹＝不是过敏性休克」——错：极少数病人唯一表现就是低血压或休克；皮肤表现并不是诊断标准的必要条件。

confusions.en: 'No wheeze means the breathing is getting better' — wrong: in a fatigued or severely obstructed patient, silence can mean almost no air is moving; a silent chest is an ominous sign, not a reassuring one.
confusions.zh: 「听不到喘鸣＝呼吸变好了」——错：疲劳或重度梗阻的病人，安静可能是因为气流几乎流不动；沉默的胸腔是危险信号，不是安心的信号。

confusions.en: 'Give the inhaler or the antihistamine first, epinephrine can wait' — wrong and a major protocol error: epinephrine reverses anaphylaxis itself; salbutamol and diphenhydramine are add-ons that only come AFTER epinephrine.
confusions.zh: 「先用吸入剂或抗组胺药，肾上腺素可以等」——错，而且是重大协议错误：肾上腺素才是逆转过敏性休克本身的药；沙丁胺醇和苯海拉明只是加分项，必须排在肾上腺素之后。

confusions.en: 'IV epinephrine is just the same drug via a different route' — wrong: IV uses the 1:10,000 concentration, 10 times more dilute than the IM 1:1,000; pushing a full 1-mL vial of the IM concentration IV is a lethal-overdose error.
confusions.zh: 「静脉肾上腺素只是换个途径，药还是一样」——错：静脉用的是 1:10,000 浓度，比肌注用的 1:1,000 稀 10 倍；把肌注浓度整支 1 mL 直接静推，是致命的过量错误。

confusions.en: 'One EpiPen dose and the danger has passed' — wrong: many reactions need more than one dose, biphasic reactions can recur hours later, and up to 20% of patients relapse within 8 hours even after apparently full recovery.
confusions.zh: 「打了一针 EpiPen 危险就过去了」——错：很多反应需要不止一次给药，双相反应可能数小时后再次发作，多达 20% 的病人在看似完全恢复后 8 小时内还会复发。

confusions.en: 'A patient on a beta blocker responds to epinephrine like anyone else' — wrong: beta blockers can blunt or even paradox the epinephrine response and mask the expected tachycardia; glucagon is the textbook rescue for these patients.
confusions.zh: 「用 β 受体阻滞剂的病人对肾上腺素反应和别人一样」——错：β 受体阻滞剂会削弱甚至反常化肾上腺素的效果，还可能掩盖本该出现的心动过速；教材给这类病人的补救药是胰高血糖素。

confusions.en: 'Corticosteroids are acute-rescue drugs for anaphylaxis' — wrong: their onset is too slow to help the immediate crisis; their theoretical role is limiting a later or biphasic reaction, not reversing the current one.
confusions.zh: 「皮质类固醇是过敏性休克的急救药」——错：起效太慢，帮不上当下的危机；它们理论上的作用是压制后续或双相反应，而不是逆转正在发生的这一次。

confusions.en: 'No personal or family history of allergy rules out anaphylaxis' — wrong: the absence of a personal or family atopy history never excludes the diagnosis.
confusions.zh: 「没有个人或家族过敏史就能排除过敏性休克」——错：个人和家族特应性病史都干净，也不能排除诊断。

confusions.en: 'A localized swelling reaction after a sting predicts anaphylaxis risk' — wrong: the source material specifically states localized reactions are NOT a risk factor for anaphylaxis; generalized urticaria after a sting is the actual red flag.
confusions.zh: 「被蜇后局部肿一块，说明容易发展成过敏性休克」——错：教材明确指出局部反应本身并不是过敏性休克的风险因素；被蜇后出现全身性荨麻疹才是真正的红旗。

mnemonics.en: BC adult epinephrine chant: 0.5 mg IM, repeat every 5 minutes, up to 3 doses.
mnemonics.zh: BC 成人肾上腺素口诀：0.5 mg 肌注，每 5 分钟重复一次，最多 3 次。

mnemonics.name: 1,000 for muscle, 10,000 for vein
mnemonics.en: The concentration matches the route: 1:1,000 goes IM, 1:10,000 goes IV — mixing them up is the classic fatal error.
mnemonics.zh: 浓度对应途径：1:1,000 走肌注，1:10,000 走静脉——搞反了就是经典的致命错误。

mnemonics.name: Epi's mirror move
mnemonics.en: Histamine dilates, leaks, bronchoconstricts, and depresses the heart; epinephrine does the exact opposite of all four at once.
mnemonics.zh: 组胺让血管扩张、渗漏、支气管收缩、心脏受抑；肾上腺素一次性把这四件事全部反过来。

mnemonics.name: Epi first, friends follow
mnemonics.en: Sequence reminder: epinephrine first, salbutamol and diphenhydramine follow — never the other way around.
mnemonics.zh: 顺序提醒：肾上腺素在前，沙丁胺醇和苯海拉明在后——绝不能反过来。

mnemonics.en: Death timing by route: about 30 minutes after eating a trigger, about 15 minutes after a sting, about 5 minutes after an injected/iatrogenic dose — the more direct the route, the faster the clock.
mnemonics.zh: 按途径记致死时间：食入约 30 分钟、叮咬约 15 分钟、注射约 5 分钟——途径越直接，倒计时越快。

mnemonics.name: 4-to-8 twice
mnemonics.en: Both the post-reaction hospital observation window and the biphasic-reaction monitoring window run about 4 to 8 hours.
mnemonics.zh: 「4 到 8」出现两次：反应后院内观察窗口和双相反应监测窗口都大约是 4-8 小时。

selfCheck.qEn: A previously healthy adult develops facial swelling and stridor 5 minutes after a wasp sting, with BP 82/50. What's the immediate BC-protocol drug, dose, route, site, and max repeats?
selfCheck.qZh: 既往健康的成人被黄蜂蜇后 5 分钟出现面部肿胀和喉鸣，血压 82/50。按 BC 协议，立即用什么药、多大剂量、什么途径、什么部位、最多重复几次？
selfCheck.aEn: Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM (1:1,000), anterolateral thigh; may repeat every 5 minutes up to 3 total doses. There is no absolute contraindication in life-threatening anaphylaxis.
selfCheck.aZh: 肾上腺素 0.5 mg 肌注（1:1,000），大腿前外侧；可每 5 分钟重复一次，最多共 3 次。危及生命的过敏性休克中肾上腺素没有绝对禁忌证。

selfCheck.qEn: How does the BC pediatric epinephrine dose differ from the adult dose, and what's the ceiling?
selfCheck.qZh: BC 儿童肾上腺素剂量和成人有什么不同？上限是多少？
selfCheck.aEn: Pediatric is weight-based: 0.01 mg/kg IM to a maximum of 0.5 mg, with the same up-to-3-doses repeat rule — the adult dose is instead fixed at 0.5 mg regardless of weight.
selfCheck.aZh: 儿童按体重算：0.01 mg/kg 肌注，上限 0.5 mg，重复规则同样最多 3 次——成人则不按体重，固定给 0.5 mg。

selfCheck.qEn: A patient in anaphylactic shock remains hypotensive after epinephrine. What's the BC fluid order?
selfCheck.qZh: 过敏性休克病人给了肾上腺素后仍然低血压，BC 的补液医嘱是什么？
selfCheck.aEn: Crystalloid bolus 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L, reassessing the patient after every 500 mL.
selfCheck.aZh: 晶体液 20 mL/kg 冲击，上限 2 L，每输 500 mL 复评一次。

selfCheck.qEn: Why does giving salbutamol or diphenhydramine before epinephrine count as a major protocol error?
selfCheck.qZh: 为什么在肾上腺素之前先给沙丁胺醇或苯海拉明算重大协议错误？
selfCheck.aEn: Neither drug reverses the anaphylactic process itself — only epinephrine addresses vasodilation, capillary leak, bronchoconstriction, and mediator release simultaneously; the others are adjuncts meant to follow epinephrine, not replace it.
selfCheck.aZh: 这两种药都不能逆转过敏性休克本身——只有肾上腺素能同时处理血管扩张、毛细血管渗漏、支气管收缩和介质释放；其他药只是辅助，该跟在肾上腺素之后，而不是替代它。

selfCheck.qEn: What two time windows should you tell a recovering anaphylaxis patient to watch for, and why?
selfCheck.qZh: 对一个正在恢复的过敏性休克病人，应该提醒他警惕哪两个时间窗？为什么？
selfCheck.aEn: A biphasic (delayed second-wave) reaction can appear hours after the first resolves, so monitor for 4-8 hours post-event; up to 20% of patients relapse within that window even after apparently full recovery.
selfCheck.aZh: 双相（延迟第二波）反应可能在第一波消退后数小时才出现，所以要监测事件后 4-8 小时；多达 20% 的病人即使看起来已完全恢复，仍会在这个窗口内复发。

selfCheck.qEn: Per BC's unstable-patient criteria, does a normotensive anaphylaxis patient still count as unstable?
selfCheck.qZh: 按 BC 的不稳定病人判定标准，一个血压正常的过敏性休克病人还算不稳定吗？
selfCheck.aEn: Yes — anaphylaxis itself is on BC's automatic unstable-findings list for the practical exam, independent of the current vital signs.
selfCheck.aZh: 算——过敏性休克本身就在 BC 实操考的自动不稳定判定清单里，跟当前生命体征无关。

bcAlerts.topicZh: 成人肾上腺素剂量公式
bcAlerts.bookEn: Weight-based formula for everyone: 0.01 mg/kg IM (max 0.5 mg adult, 0.3 mg pediatric), repeatable every 5-15 minutes.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材对所有人都用按体重公式：0.01 mg/kg 肌注（成人上限 0.5 mg，儿童上限 0.3 mg），可每 5-15 分钟重复。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC fixes the adult dose instead: 0.5 mg IM flat, repeatable every 5 minutes up to 3 doses total; only the pediatric dose keeps the 0.01 mg/kg (max 0.5 mg) weight-based formula. Answer with BC's fixed adult number.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 把成人剂量固定死了：0.5 mg 肌注、每 5 分钟可重复、最多共 3 次；只有儿童剂量保留 0.01 mg/kg（上限 0.5 mg）的按体重公式。答题以 BC 的固定成人数字为准。

bcAlerts.topicEn: IV epinephrine as an anaphylaxis route
bcAlerts.topicZh: 静脉肾上腺素作为过敏性休克给药途径
bcAlerts.bookEn: Discusses diluting the 1:10,000 vial for an IV bolus (0.05-0.1 mg) or running an infusion (1-4 mcg/min) in refractory or peri-arrest anaphylaxis.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材讨论把 1:10,000 稀释后静推（0.05-0.1 mg）或持续输注（1-4 mcg/min），用于难治性或濒临骤停的过敏性休克。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's Epinephrine monograph lists Route: IM only, with no IV route documented for this drug at PCP scope. Treat the book's IV-epinephrine content as background theory, not the exam answer, for an anaphylaxis stem — IM stays the answer.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 的肾上腺素药物单只写「途径：肌注」，PCP 权限下没有为这个药记录静脉途径。教材里静脉肾上腺素的内容当背景知识记住即可，过敏性休克题的考试答案仍然是肌注。

bcAlerts.topicZh: 过敏性休克低血压的补液量
bcAlerts.bookEn: Roughly 1-2 L of crystalloid up front, escalating to a vasopressor if there's no response after 3-4 L.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材：前期大约给 1-2 L 晶体液，超过 3-4 L 仍无反应就升级到升压药。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC uses the same weight-based formula as its general hypovolemia protocol: 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L, reassessing every 500 mL. Answer with this formula, not the book's fixed litre range.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 用和低血容量休克协议相同的按体重公式：20 mL/kg，上限 2 L，每 500 mL 复评一次。答题用这个公式，不用教材固定的升数区间。

bcAlerts.topicZh: 胰高血糖素的适应证范围
bcAlerts.bookEn: Recommends glucagon 1-5 mg IV over 5 minutes (then a 5-15 mg/min infusion) specifically as an anaphylaxis rescue drug for beta-blocker patients who don't respond to epinephrine.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材推荐胰高血糖素 1-5 mg 静注、用时 5 分钟（之后可 5-15 mg/min 输注），专门用于对肾上腺素无反应的 β 阻滞剂病人。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's Glucagon monograph lists indications only as hypoglycemia and failed IV access — anaphylaxis/beta-blocker rescue is not a listed BC indication. Don't answer 'give glucagon' as the exam response to a beta-blocker anaphylaxis stem; the exam answer stays IM epinephrine (repeated per protocol) plus supportive care.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 的胰高血糖素药物单适应证只写低血糖和静脉通路开不上——没有把过敏性休克/β 阻滞剂补救列为适应证。遇到 β 阻滞剂过敏性休克的考题，不要答「给胰高血糖素」，考试答案仍是按协议重复肌注肾上腺素加支持治疗。

bcAlerts.topicEn: Anaphylaxis as an automatic unstable finding
bcAlerts.topicZh: 过敏性休克自动判不稳定
bcAlerts.bookEn: No equivalent single checklist — severity is judged case by case from the clinical picture.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材没有对应的单一判定清单——严重度靠逐例判断临床表现来定。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's 'Findings in Unstable Adult Patients' list for the practical exam names anaphylaxis explicitly — it is always treated and transported as unstable RTC regardless of the current vital signs.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 实操考的「成人不稳定表现」清单明确列出「过敏性休克」——无论当前生命体征如何，一律按不稳定 RTC 处理和转运。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Guidelines p.7 Findings in Unstable Adult Patients

bcAlerts.topicZh: 强制要求的现场非药物操作顺序
bcAlerts.bookEn: General ABC framing with no explicit ordered checklist before drug administration.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材只有笼统的 ABC 框架，给药前没有明确的分步清单。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's Anaphylaxis guideline spells out the order explicitly: position supine and never walk the patient, remove the allergen, complete a primary survey with O2 to keep SpO2 at or above 94%, delegate a crew member to prep egress, obtain history and baseline vitals — THEN administer epinephrine.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 过敏性休克指南把顺序写得很明确：仰卧、绝不让病人走动，移除过敏原，完成初评并给氧维持 SpO2 ≥94%，指派搭档准备撤离路线，采集病史和基线生命体征——然后才给肾上腺素。
